Name: Leah
Transcript: Thanks for doing this. There are no right or wrong answers, it's your experience I'm interested in, and we can stop whenever you like. So, to start. Can you tell me how you came to be working from home, and what it's like for you now?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: So I'm an HR adviser, for a supermarket chain, head office side, not in a store. And in March 2020 we were all sent home with our laptops and, you know, it'll be a few weeks. And then the office lease came up and they just didn't renew it. So now there's a hub in Leeds you can book a desk at, but it's an hour and a half each way, so nobody does. So I'm home. Full time. What's it like now? Erm. It's good and it's not good. I think that's the honest answer. I'm there for the kids in a way I couldn't have been. And I'm also never not at work. Both of those are true.

Name: Leah
Transcript: Never not at work. Can you say a bit more about that?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: It's that the laptop is on the dining table. So it's there when I'm doing breakfast, it's there when we eat tea, it's there at nine o'clock at night when I come back down after bedtime. And it's very easy to just lift the lid. Just to check. And then it's ten o'clock and I've answered six emails that could have waited till the morning, and I'm wired, and I can't sleep.

Name: Leah
Transcript: Can you take me through a normal working day, from when you get up?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: Okay. So, alarm's at half six. Lewis, my husband, he's up and in the spare room by quarter to eight, because he's got a stand-up at eight with his team in India, so that's sort of fixed. So the kids are mine in the morning. Breakfast, uniforms, Tomi can't find a shoe, every single day he can't find a shoe. I walk them to school, which honestly is the nicest bit of my day. Then I come back, and I put the kettle on, and I sit down at the table, and I'm at work. Usually by quarter past nine. I'm meant to start at nine but, you know. Then it's calls, mostly. Managers ringing about a disciplinary or someone's sick note. Lunch, if I have it, is standing up. And then at three I'm off to get them, and I'm back on from about half four while they have the telly on, which I'm not proud of. And then after bedtime, the lid.

Name: Leah
Transcript: You said you're not proud of the telly.

Name: Kemi
Transcript: No. Well. It's that I'm here. So it looks like I'm with them. But I'm not with them, I'm in the next room with my headset on telling someone their probation's been extended. My daughter said to me once, Mummy, are you at work or at home? And I said, I'm at home, darling. And she said, no, but are you at work. Seven years old. She'd got it exactly.

Name: Leah
Transcript: Where in your home do you work? What's that space like for you?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: The dining table. Which, we don't really have a dining room, it's the end of the kitchen. So it's the kitchen table. And it was a thing, when we started, that Lewis would have the spare room because his calls are more, he's on calls all day with people in different countries and it needs to be quiet. And I'm on calls too. Quite sensitive calls, actually. Someone crying because they've been signed off with stress, and then the washing machine goes into its spin. So it doesn't really work. But it got decided in the first week, when it was going to be a few weeks, and then it just stayed decided.

Name: Leah
Transcript: How was it decided?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: I don't think it was. That's the thing. Nobody sat down. It was just, his job's the big job. He earns more, so. That's not something either of us has ever said out loud. But it's sort of in the house, isn't it. It's in who gets the door that shuts.

Name: Leah
Transcript: What happens at the start and the end of your working day?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: Started is easy, started is when I get back from the school gate. That walk back is my commute, I suppose. Ten minutes. I sometimes go the long way round the park just to have it. Finished is the problem. Finished doesn't really happen. I tried, I had a little thing where at half five I'd close the laptop and put it in the sideboard. Like, out of sight. And I did that for about two weeks, and then there was a restructure and I needed it in the evenings, and it never went back in the sideboard. It just lives on the table now.

Name: Leah
Transcript: What was it like, those two weeks?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: Lovely, actually. I'd forgotten that. It felt like closing a shop. The table was a table again. We had tea on it without having to move the charger.

Name: Leah
Transcript: How has working from home changed things with the people you live with, or the people around you?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: Well, with the kids, I see them more, and that's real, I don't want to take that away. I do the school run both ends, which before I never did. My mum used to do pick-ups for us, and she's not getting any younger, so that's a relief. With Lewis, it's harder to say. I think because I'm at home and I'm in the kitchen, everything that happens in the house kind of comes to me. The parcels, the boiler man, the dentist ringing. Because I'm here. He's here too, he's just upstairs, but upstairs is work and downstairs is home, somehow. Even though I'm working downstairs. Does that make sense?

Name: Leah
Transcript: It does. Can you tell me about a time that happened?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: There was a day, last month, I was in a meeting with a regional manager, quite a tense one, and the doorbell went, and it was a delivery for Lewis. Something for his bike. And I had to say, sorry, can you give me two seconds, and go and sign for it. And then I came back and the manager had lost his train of thought, and I felt really unprofessional. And Lewis came down at lunch and said, oh, did my thing come? And I wanted to throw it at him. Which was unfair, because he'd have answered it if I'd asked. But I'd have had to go up and ask. And he never has to come down and ask.

Name: Leah
Transcript: Can you tell me about a day working from home that has stayed with you?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: It's not one day, it's more a kind of day. The doorbell, that's one. But the big one is when one of the kids is ill. Before, if Tomi was ill, one of us had to take a day off, and it was a proper conversation, whose day it was going to be. Now he just stays at home with me. On the sofa, with a bucket. And I work. And I'm not working well and I'm not looking after him well. And nobody at work says take the day off, because why would you, you're at home. And I don't say it either. I just do both, badly.

Name: Leah
Transcript: What do you do with that feeling, of doing both badly?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: Nothing, really. Carry it round. I think if anyone asked me, I'd say I'm very lucky. And I am. Most of the women I went to school with would love to be able to work at home with their kids. So you don't feel you can complain. You've got the thing everyone wanted.

Name: Leah
Transcript: What, if anything, do you miss about working somewhere else? And what would you miss if you had to go back?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: The train. This is going to sound mad. I miss the train. It was forty minutes into Sheffield, and it was the only forty minutes in my day when nobody needed anything from me. I could read a book. I read so many books on that train. I don't think I've finished a book since 2020. And I miss, there was a woman in payroll, Denise, we used to have a sandwich together on a Friday. Just that. And I didn't know it was holding me up until it wasn't there. What would I miss if I went back? The school gate. Without a doubt. My daughter runs out and she's looking for me, and I'm there. I couldn't give that up now. I think I'd rather be lonely.

Name: Leah
Transcript: Is there anything about working from home that we haven't touched on, that matters to you?

Name: Kemi
Transcript: I think just that it's not one thing. People ask, do you like working from home, and they want a yes or a no. And it's more, I've got a different life. Some of it's better and some of it's worse, and it's all mixed up together on one table.
